name: Ollama (local models)
notes: Not a coding agent. Ollama serves models; an agent adapter points at it. Listed here so a role can be assigned a local model by name, and because the economics differ enough to change which roles are worth running: no quota, no per-token cost, no network — but a smaller model and a shorter context.

hosts.note: Agents that can be pointed at an Ollama endpoint instead of a hosted provider.
hosts.opencode: provider config; installed on this machine

good_for: normalising tracker items into the inbox schema
classifying an item's shape (slice vs project) as a first pass
summarising a transcript for a status line
not_for: writing acceptance boundaries — admission is a judgement call and the whole gate
why: The cheap roles are high-volume and low-stakes: fifty issues normalised into one schema costs a frontier model real quota and asks nothing a local model cannot do. The expensive roles are the opposite — one decision, and being wrong is costly. Splitting them is what makes an unattended queue affordable.
